notes: Verification pass, session 10 (D-61 section 1; D-61 addendum point 7). An archived capture of the operator's own sheet (D-61, 1a), opened by the session from the archive: 'CyrusOne Data Center San Antonio I, 9999 Westover Hills Blvd | San Antonio, TX 78251 ... Two 200MW substations provide power to the site ... Regulated utility provider - CPS Energy'. utility_source_site_identity: documents.cyrusone.com and cyrusone.com are the operator's own domain (its Form 8-K exhibit, as above)
utility_evidence_period: sheets of 2018 and 2022, as captured in December 2022 and December 2023
notes: Verification pass, session 10 (D-61 section 1; D-61 addendum point 7). The operator's own sheet, in an archived capture from its own domain (D-61, 1a), which also establishes the provenance of the directory-hosted copy (1b: the same file by hash). 'CyrusOne Data Center Cincinnati - Hamilton, 103 Knightsbridge Drive, Hamilton, OH 45011 ... this 83,000 square foot facility ... This "green" data center utilizes power from the city that is 45% from a non-carbon source. The site has 4.8 MW total available power'. Flagged: 'the city' is not named. It is read as the City of Hamilton, the sheet's own city, which runs a municipal electric system; that Cincinnati has no city electric utility is general knowledge and is said so. Support, on file: the City of Hamilton's 2014 brochure says its electric grid serves Vora Technology Park from three city substations (no page opened ties this address to the park). Ohio's service-area layer returns Duke Energy Ohio at the point and holds no municipal systems, so it cannot speak to this (D-61, 2c). Delivery or sale: a city's own system delivers what it sells. Coverage: the sheet is for the whole building. Period: 2018 to 2023; the 2012 sheet names no source of power. The row is dated 2011 and its host's crossing is 2012, so reading this for those years is ruling 4's standing assumption.

site_name: CyrusOne Lewisville, Convergence Office Center, 2501 S State Hwy 121
serving_utility: Texas-New Mexico Power (TNMP), the wires company
notes: Verification pass, session 10 (D-61 section 1; D-61 addendum point 7). Replaces the record in batch_c_1.json, whose source was a news portal's copy of the operator's wire release. Under D-61's 1b a republished release needs its provenance, and neither the wire service's own copy nor a copy on the operator's site was found (the Internet Archive's listing of the wire's pages for 25 February 2013 has none for this operator; the operator's archived Lewisville sheets of 2012, 2015 and 2019 name no utility). So the record now rests on dated trade press, opened by the session: Data Center Knowledge, 11 March 2013, 'The Lewisville site, in the Dallas market, now has 25 MVA of redundant utility capacity from Texas New Mexico Power', followed by a quotation from the operator's vice president of data center design and construction, named. The republished release (ca.style.yahoo.com/2013-02-25-global-colocation-solutions-provider-cyrusone-upgr.html) carries the same figure and utility and is kept as a lead beside it. Delivery or sale: TNMP is a wires company and delivers. Coverage: 'the facility's total'. Period: early 2013. The state's project record EABPRJA9809204 ties the facility to 2501 State Hwy 121. TNMP is outside the panel (D-4), so the site leaves Denton County Electric Cooperative, where the map had put it.
